structural_score_basis: Adopted 4.0/10 for the staged dashboard, replacing the unrated state rather than mechanically restoring historical 6.0. The binding weakness is the accepted active 2-of-3 Council path into core issuance: at the eligible pinned state it can expand the full 310m facilitator capacity to 620m and then mint without a DAO queue. The additional 310m is next-update headroom, not a permanent lifetime ceiling; repeated eligible updates can increase capacity further. The one-day DAO floor and separate 5-of-9 guardian protect the queued DAO route, not this immediate Council path. Source-bound core contracts, published reviews and code-enforced per-update limits are real positives, so this is not treated as proof of active exploitation or unconstrained outsider minting. Nevertheless, intended privileged capability is a material compromise/misuse exposure. Partial audit-to-deployment coverage, operational fee-accrual remediation and remote bridge/token/role-history gaps limit code confidence. The halves are not averaged: audit history cannot offset the immediate core mint capability. This score prices the combined Contract & Admin axis only; Dependencies 6.0 and Issuer 6.5 are unchanged. This is a Codex-authored combined assessment adopted by the user for the staged dashboard; it is not a finding of realized loss or authorization to publish.
